To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the temporal difference method is an effective tool for policy evaluation in the context of MDPs and POMDPs, and that the temporal difference algorithm is a simple and efficient tool for policy evaluation.

(1) the performance of TD learning algorithms is strongly affected by the choice of the learning rate and discount factor, (2) the choice of the TD learning method is also important, and (3) there is a tradeoff between the speed of learning and the quality of the final solution.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How can a robot learn from experience to solve new problems? How can it learn to perform a task from a human teacher? How can we design robots that can adapt to new situations?
the problem of evaluating and comparing the performance of reinforcement learning algorithms for policy evaluation and control in the context of Markov decision processes.
the design and evaluation of reinforcement learning (RL) methods for solving Markov Decision Processes (MDPs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the temporal difference learning algorithm is an efficient way of approximating the value of a policy, but it is not the only way to do so, nor is it the only way to approximate the policy itself.
the temporal difference learning methods are not a panacea for all problems.
the temporal difference methods are not the best methods in the world for solving MDP problems, but they are the best methods for solving large MDP problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a new method to solve the problem of the optimal control in a stochastic environment.
we have proposed a novel method to evaluate policies in reinforcement learning.
we have proposed a new approach to model and solve POMDPs, and have shown that our method is effective in solving a variety of problems in robotics and planning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the temporal-difference method to evaluate policies for POMDPs.
, for the first time, we can now evaluate the performance of an RL policy on a task without having to execute it on an actual robot.

, in the context of policy evaluation with TD methods, the choice of whether to use an on-policy or off-policy TD method is not a matter of theoretical purity or practical convenience but a fundamental design decision with significant consequences.
